### Summary

Dyad is a free Lovable alternative that changes the AI app-building paradigm. It operates as an open-source, local-first desktop application, ensuring complete user control and privacy. This architecture stands in contrast to the cloud-based, freemium models of its competitors, which often come with limited free tiers and vendor lock-in.

| Architecture | Local-First, Open-Source, Desktop App | Cloud-Based, Proprietary, Web App |
| Data Privacy | Private; your code is stored on your computer | Your code is stored on the Cloud |

### Key Differences [...] ### Key Differences

Understanding the distinctions in philosophy and functionality reveals why so many are choosing Dyad as their go-to free Lovable alternative.

1. Local-First vs. Cloud-Based

 Dyad: Operates directly on your machine. This local-first design is the cornerstone of its appeal, offering inherent privacy and flexibility. Your project is yours, from the first line of code to the last.
 Bolt, v0.dev, & Lovable: Function as cloud services. While convenient, this model means your data is processed on external servers, and your workflow is dependent on a good internet connection and the provider's uptime.

## Local-first + BYOK, explained

Open Design runs a desktop app, a local daemon, and Markdown skill and design-system catalogs on your machine. No design output is forced through a vendor cloud, and your brand lives in your repo as a portable DESIGN.md file every skill respects.

You bring your own agent key. Credentials stay in local config or environment variables — Open Design never proxies them — and the API spend bills directly to you.

## Is there a free, open-source Lovable alternative?

Yes. Open Design is free and open-source — Apache-2.0, BYOK, so the app costs nothing and you pay only your own provider API spend — and is the design-first option. Dyad (Apache-2.0) is the other open-source option: a local app builder you can run for free. 3. Export and validate data. Compare record counts, relationships, timestamps, and file manifests.
4. Rotate secrets. Recreate API keys and OAuth credentials rather than copying them into a new uncontrolled environment.
5. Rebuild authentication carefully. Test account linking, password resets, email verification, sessions, and authorization rules.
6. Choose hosting and observability. Add logs, metrics, error reporting, backups, and an incident owner.

## Other Lovable alternatives

### Replit

Replit is the closest all-in-one alternative among mainstream builders because it combines a browser IDE, Agent, runtime, database, and deployment. It also uses subscriptions, effort-based agent work, and integrated infrastructure, so it is a convenience move rather than an ownership move (Replit pricing explanation).

### OpenHands

OpenHands provides an MIT-licensed software-agent core with local and Docker deployment paths (OpenHands repository). It is powerful for technical teams but does not reproduce Lovable's visual prompt-to-app polish.
